title: ACL Reconstruction Recovery: What Each Stage Looks Like
seo_title: ACL Reconstruction Recovery Stages | Elite Sports Medicine
description: Recovery after ACL reconstruction runs in stages: movement, strength, control, then sport. What each involves, and why return to sport is decided by testing.
body_html:
ACL reconstruction itself is the shorter half of the job. What decides the result is the rehabilitation that follows, and it runs in stages rather than on a fixed calendar. Here is what to expect from each one.

Before surgery

Rehabilitation often starts before the operation, to settle the swelling and get the knee moving again. An exam and an MRI come first, because ACL tears often arrive with a meniscus tear or bruising of the bone, and anything found alongside the ligament is treated as part of the same plan.

The operation

The torn ligament is replaced with a graft, using minimally invasive arthroscopic technique. The graft is either your own tissue or donor tissue. Which one suits you comes down to your age, how hard you load the knee and what exactly was damaged.

The stages of rehab

  1. Movement. Rehab starts almost straight away, getting the knee bending and straightening again.
  2. Strength. Rebuilding the muscles that protect the knee.
  3. Control. Proprioception and neuromuscular control: the coordination and reaction time that keep the knee in line when you land or change direction.
  4. Sport-specific work. The movements your knee actually has to survive in your sport or job. Skip this stage and a knee can test well in clinic and fail on the field.

A brace is often used early on, and again when you start returning to sport, depending on how stable the knee is.

How long it takes

Everyday activity comes back within a few months for most people. Return to pivoting sport commonly takes around nine months or more.

That return is decided by testing, not the calendar: strength, control, movement quality and hop symmetry. Reaching a date is not the same as being ready for a cut, a landing or a tackle.

Is surgery always needed?

Not always. A completely torn ACL does not heal back together by itself, but some less active people do well with rehabilitation and changes to how they use the knee. For most active people who want to return to cutting and pivoting sport, reconstruction is the most reliable path back to a stable knee. The ACL tear page covers how that decision is made.
